options.feedback: Extreme unsupervised restriction is not a substitute for measured decongestion and can reduce preload excessively. Use a monitored plan tailored to volume status.
options.patientWrong: Nothing to drink and nothing to remove the swelling. … Severe, but not precise.
options.fennWrong: Manage volume with measurements, not absolutes.

management.quote: “The shoes fit again. … A modest but meaningful victory.”

management.title: Choose disease-targeted therapy
management.openingFenn: The workup supports idiopathic PAH; vasoreactivity is negative and she is not in overt shock.
management.hint: Use risk assessment and initial combination therapy appropriate for a treatment-naive patient without major cardiopulmonary comorbidity.
management.hintPatient: Two pathways. … I suppose one medication would be aesthetically cleaner, but medicine rarely consults me.
management.prompt: Which initial targeted strategy is most appropriate at the specialist centre?
management.promptRemark: I would like the treatment plan now. Preferably before another staircase appears.

options.text: High-dose calcium-channel blocker monotherapy
options.feedback: High-dose calcium-channel blockers are reserved for the small minority with a positive acute vasoreactivity test and durable response. Her test is negative, so empiric treatment could worsen haemodynamics.
options.patientWrong: My mother took one of those. … My test, however, was negative.
options.fennWrong: Vasoreactivity is the gate; she did not pass it.

options.text: Anticoagulation as the sole PAH treatment
options.feedback: Routine anticoagulation is not a substitute for pulmonary vascular therapy and is individualized because benefit and bleeding risk vary. It does not lower pulmonary vascular resistance by itself.
options.patientWrong: A thinner blood supply facing the same resistance. … Incomplete.
options.fennWrong: An adjunct in selected patients cannot replace targeted vasodilator therapy.

options.text: Begin an endothelin-receptor antagonist plus a PDE-5 inhibitor with specialist risk follow-up
options.feedback: Correct. For treatment-naive idiopathic PAH without major cardiopulmonary comorbidity at low or intermediate risk, initial ERA plus PDE-5 inhibitor therapy is recommended. Reassess risk early; inadequate response or high-risk features should prompt escalation, including parenteral prostacyclin consideration.
options.patientCorrect: Two medications. Daily. … I will have a cabinet made for them.

options.text: Use inhaled corticosteroid and a rescue bronchodilator
options.feedback: Normal spirometry and absent airway symptoms argue against asthma, and inhaled therapy does not lower the fixed pulmonary vascular resistance shown on catheterization.
options.patientWrong: An inhaler for normal airways. … Decorative, perhaps.
options.fennWrong: The obstruction is vascular, not bronchial.

management.quote: “A two-drug plan. … Proportionate, apparently.”

management.title: Plan monitoring and escalation
management.openingFenn: A prescription is not the endpoint; risk changes over time.
management.hint: Follow symptoms, functional class, exercise capacity, natriuretic peptide, echocardiographic right-heart function, and haemodynamics when indicated.
management.hintPatient: You are scheduling my future rather aggressively. … Sensible.
management.prompt: What is the appropriate ongoing plan?
management.promptRemark: I assume this requires more than an annual polite inquiry.

options.text: Return in one year if symptoms persist
options.feedback: PAH requires early structured reassessment because clinical worsening may be subtle and treatment escalation is risk-driven. A one-year gap is unsafe in newly diagnosed symptomatic disease.
options.patientWrong: A year. … I deteriorated while being patient for two.
options.fennWrong: Risk must be reassessed before another long adaptation becomes invisible.

options.text: Stop therapy once ankle swelling resolves
options.feedback: Oedema is one consequence of right-heart strain, not a marker that pulmonary vascular disease has resolved. Stopping targeted therapy risks clinical worsening.
options.patientWrong: My ankles are not the entire pulmonary circulation. … Even I know that.
options.fennWrong: Decongestion is not cure.

options.text: Use symptoms alone and avoid objective reassessment
options.feedback: Patients can unconsciously reduce activity and report stability while disease progresses—the pattern that delayed her presentation. Objective functional and right-heart measures are essential.
options.patientWrong: I redesigned my day around the breathlessness. … Symptoms alone were clearly unreliable.
options.fennWrong: Her adaptation is exactly why objective risk markers matter.

options.text: Arrange early multidisciplinary reassessment and escalate therapy according to risk
options.feedback: Correct. Follow her at a pulmonary-hypertension centre with functional class, exercise capacity, biomarkers, right-ventricular assessment, and medication monitoring. Escalate promptly for intermediate-high or high-risk status and consider transplant evaluation when response remains inadequate.
options.patientCorrect: I see. … My husband will worry. Good. He widened the stairs.

management.quote: “A specialist, a schedule, and objective measures. … Acceptable.”

hints.fenn: Clear lungs, loud P2, elevated JVP, and a right-ventricular heave describe pressure overload on the right side.
hints.patient: The right side has become the subject of the evening.

hints.fenn: The ECG, natriuretic peptide, and isolated low diffusion capacity support a pulmonary vascular process; echo should estimate probability next.
hints.patient: A sequence. … I appreciate sequences.

hints.fenn: Echo can suggest the disorder, but right-heart catheterization confirms the pre-capillary haemodynamics.
hints.patient: The invasive test is the decisive one. … Unfortunate, but clear.

hints.fenn: Before calling it idiopathic, exclude chronic thromboembolic disease and associated systemic causes.
hints.patient: Idiopathic should mean unexplained, not uninvestigated.

debrief.title: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension with Right-Heart Strain
debrief.pearl: Progressive exertional dyspnoea, exertional near-syncope, loud P2, RV heave, elevated JVP, right-heart strain, and clear lungs suggest pulmonary hypertension. Echocardiography estimates probability; right-heart catheterization confirms and classifies haemodynamics. Exclude secondary causes, treat congestion carefully, begin risk-appropriate PAH therapy in an expert centre, and reassess risk early.
